package_info.why_malicious: Vulnerable versions of Drupal Core allow authenticated users to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of another user's session via a reflected DOM XSS in rejected forms, leading to account hijacking and malicious content injection.

execution_context.trigger: form submission with expired/invalid CSRF token (rejected form)
execution_context.file_location: node/add/[type] and node/[node-id]/edit endpoints (form handler, CKEditor integration)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a form is submitted with an expired CSRF token, the posted content (including malicious HTML/JS) is reflected in the error page and rendered by CKEditor, which executes the injected JavaScript in the user's browser context.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows user-supplied HTML/JS to be reflected and executed in the browser, enabling XSS attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, user input should be sanitized and not allow script execution, especially in error or rejected form states. Here, the input is reflected unsanitized.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be reflecting user content for recovery after form rejection, but not executing scripts.
key_indicators: User input reflected unsanitized in HTML context
Bypass of CKEditor script filtering via iframe embedding

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a POST request to node/add/[type] or node/[node-id]/edit with malicious HTML/JS in a CKEditor-enabled field (e.g., body[0][value]), using Full HTML mode.
attack_chain.leads_to: Form is rejected due to missing/invalid CSRF token, but the malicious content is reflected in the error page.

attack_chain.action: CKEditor on the error page renders the reflected content, including the injected <iframe> and <script> tags.
attack_chain.leads_to: Injected JavaScript executes in the victim's browser context.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript can hijack user sessions, steal credentials, or inject further malicious content.
attack_chain.leads_to: Account compromise, data theft, or further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Reflection of user-supplied HTML/JS in error or rejected form pages
Execution of script tags in CKEditor fields after form rejection
Presence of <iframe> and <script> tags in form field values
file_indicators: node/add/* and node/*/edit endpoints with error messages reflecting form content
CKEditor-enabled fields (e.g., body[0][value]) containing suspicious HTML/JS
network_indicators: Unusual POST requests to node/add/* or node/*/edit with HTML/JS payloads
Subsequent requests or actions triggered by injected JavaScript (e.g., credential exfiltration endpoints)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for POST requests to content creation/edit endpoints with HTML/JS payloads in CKEditor fields, especially when followed by form rejection errors. Inspect error pages for unsanitized reflection of user input. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to block script tags in form fields, and audit CKEditor configuration for proper script filtering.
